about: Anti-slop rules for AI-made work, by context. They are design and writing preferences, not a test of who or what made something: judge the result, never guess the author. The rules draw on several sources (see Sources in SKILL.md and NOTICE). 'dont' is the pattern; 'instead' is what to do.

contexts.app: App and dashboard UI, HTML prototypes
contexts.doc: Documents and reports (research write-ups, PDFs, briefs)
contexts.copy: Social and marketing copy (posts, captions, emails, ads)
contexts.code: Code (JavaScript, TypeScript, Python): source files and diffs

check_kinds.machine: A static checker can find it in HTML, CSS, Markdown, text or JS/TS/Python source (check-slop.mjs). A hit is evidence, not a verdict.
check_kinds.screenshot: Needs the rendered result: look at a screenshot at 390, 820 and 1280 px.
check_kinds.judgement: Needs a person or a model reviewing against the brief and brand.

rules.dont: Every hero uses an indigo/violet gradient on a white page. Do not fall back to purple gradients on white backgrounds.
rules.instead: Pick a palette from a real reference style and commit to it; use gradients only where they mean something.

rules.dont: Purple or violet gradients, cyan on dark, or flat neon on dark (the AI colour palette).
rules.instead: Use a deliberate, content-led palette; preserve intentional brand styling.

rules.dont: One default sans for headings, body and buttons; Inter for the entire interface.
rules.instead: Pair a characterful display face with a readable body font; match the type to the brand's mood.

rules.dont: Defaulting to Inter, Roboto, Fraunces, Geist, Plus Jakarta Sans or Space Grotesk.
rules.instead: Choose fonts to suit the brand, not by default. A project or brand font chosen on purpose is fine: record why.

rules.dont: Impact, Arial Black or a standard system sans for headlines.
rules.instead: Choose a deliberate headline font that fits the brand.

rules.dont: The same five-block landing page for every product: a "new" badge, a centred hero, feature cards, a stats band, pricing, logos, an FAQ and a big footer, in that order. (Flag it when three or more of these appear together.)
rules.instead: Design around the content: editorial spreads, bento grids, a single bold statement, a product demo.

rules.dont: 🚀 ✨ 💡 sprinkled in headings and feature lists; emoji as interface icons.
rules.instead: Use one consistent icon set, custom illustrations, or none at all.

rules.dont: Identical large radius and soft shadow on every card and button; hairline border plus a wide soft shadow across a row of cards.
rules.instead: Choose a shape language deliberately: sharp, pill, or mixed, and apply it with intent. Use restrained elevation or borders.

rules.dont: Frosted glass panels over plain backgrounds where nothing shows through.
rules.instead: Use blur only over rich imagery; otherwise solid surfaces read better.

rules.dont: "Unlock your potential with our revolutionary AI-powered platform." Plus the usual suspects: elevate, seamless, supercharge, unleash, empower, next-generation, and "Welcome back, Sam ✨" on every screen.
rules.instead: Write specific, concrete headlines about what the product does for whom.

rules.dont: Every section is centered text in a narrow column; an off-white background with everything centered.
rules.instead: Use left-aligned text, asymmetric grids, and varied section layouts.

rules.dont: "10,000+ happy customers" and stock-photo quotes from Jane D.; a decorative big-number hero metric.
rules.instead: Leave them out until real ones exist, or show real product proof and only real relevant metrics.

rules.dont: Light gray body text on white; text too faint to pass contrast; gray text on a colored background.
rules.instead: Meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text); let hierarchy come from size and weight, not faded color. Tint secondary text from the background hue.

rules.dont: bg-clip-text gradients on all headings; gradient fill on text, especially headings and numbers.
rules.instead: Reserve special treatments for one hero moment.

rules.dont: Floating abstract 3D shapes with no relation to the product; a big illustration built from basic shapes.
rules.instead: Show the actual product, real photography, or purpose-made illustration.

rules.dont: Uniform padding makes every section feel equally important; the same spacing everywhere.
rules.instead: Use rhythm: tight groups, generous breaks, and deliberate density changes.

rules.dont: Slate gray, default radius, default buttons.
rules.instead: Retheme tokens: colors, fonts, radius, borders, to match a chosen style.

rules.dont: The same thin-line icon library every AI-built site uses, straight out of the box; mixed icon styles.
rules.instead: Pick an icon style that suits the brand, or customize stroke weight and corners. Use one cohesive set.

rules.dont: "Get started" and "Learn more" side by side, same size, same weight.
rules.instead: One clear main button; make the second option a quiet text link.

rules.dont: A grid of rounded tiles as the automatic second section; identical card rows; cards inside cards; an icon in a box above every heading.
rules.instead: Only use tiles when the content really comes in tile-sized pieces; let real content determine the layout. Flatten nested cards.

rules.dont: Huge but hairline-thin headline text, sometimes faded to low opacity.
rules.instead: Give the headline enough weight and contrast to carry the page.

rules.dont: Buttons filled with a two-tone gradient.
rules.instead: Solid buttons in the brand color; save gradients for one deliberate moment, if any.

rules.dont: Flawless smiling faces that could belong to any company.
rules.instead: Real photos of real people, or no people at all.

rules.dont: A struck-through price next to a loud discount badge that sits on the pricing card forever.
rules.instead: Show the real price plainly; only show a discount badge for a real, time-limited offer.

rules.dont: A row of shouty all-caps phrases separated by ✦ sparkles, often running as a strip or ticker; text that scrolls by itself.
rules.instead: Let one clear headline do the work; set a short list in normal case with plain separators.

rules.dont: Three pricing cards with the middle one raised, highlighted and tagged "Most popular" by default.
rules.instead: Lay out the plans evenly; only highlight one when you actually know it's the one most people pick.

rules.dont: A newsletter pop-up, a chat bubble, a back-to-top button and a floating badge all following you down the page.
rules.instead: Keep only the navigation fixed (plus one action bar on phones); put the newsletter signup in the footer.

rules.dont: Form fields where the only hint is grey text inside the box, which disappears as soon as you start typing.
rules.instead: Give every field a visible label above it that stays put, like "Email" or "Arrival date".

rules.dont: "Book a call" in the nav, twice in the hero and again in a banner, all visible at once.
rules.instead: Show the main button once in the nav and once in the hero, and at most two buttons in the hero.

rules.dont: A "Trusted by" strip of logos the AI drew itself: wobbly look-alikes of real brands, or companies that don't exist.
rules.instead: Only show logos of real clients, using their official files. No clients yet? Leave the strip out.

rules.dont: Every card's description chopped off mid-sentence with "…" so all the cards line up.
rules.instead: Write shorter text that fits, or let each card grow to fit its words. Never cut off the part people need to read.

rules.dont: "Acme Inc", "Jane Doe", "you@example.com" and a copyright year that's long gone, still sitting on the live site.
rules.instead: Before you publish, look through every page for placeholder names, emails and dates, and swap in your own.

rules.dont: Every card, icon and badge gets its own bright color, so no color means anything.
rules.instead: Pick one main color, one supporting color and one accent, and use them roughly 60/30/10. Give the accent a job, like the main button.

rules.dont: Pulsing "Active", "Live" or "Verified" chips that never change, or that nothing actually checks; a pulsing live dot that isn't showing live data.
rules.instead: Only show a status when it can change and you're showing the real thing. If it's always true, leave it out.

rules.dont: Icons, bullets and list text sitting a few pixels off each other.
rules.instead: Line every icon up with the middle of its first line of text, and keep the same gap between icon and text on every row.

rules.dont: "// features" or "/* about us */" above the headings of a site that has nothing to do with code; decorative monospace.
rules.instead: Write a plain heading. Save code styling for actual code.

rules.dont: "Built with React and Tailwind", "Powered by AI" or a slogan like "one campus. one app.": words that came from the chat that built the site, not from the business.
rules.instead: Read every line as a customer would. If it describes how the site was made instead of what you do for them, cut it.

rules.dont: Large elements made pill-shaped; pill-shaped buttons.
rules.instead: Reserve pills for small tags; use straight or subtly rounded corners consistently; card radii around 12–16px.

rules.dont: Meaningless sparklines, progress rings or soft rounded boxes filling empty space.
rules.instead: Show real content or leave useful breathing room.

rules.dont: Fake hand-drawn doodles or fake grain as generic decoration; decorative repeating stripes; blob or torn-edge image shapes; photos in arbitrary shape cut-outs.
rules.instead: Use genuine source imagery or purpose-made artwork and clean crops.

rules.dont: Light or dark mode chosen just because the category usually does; warm cream by default.
rules.instead: Choose the viewing mode and background for the audience, content and environment.

rules.dont: The same fade-in everywhere; bouncy or elastic animation; a blinking cursor with nothing to type.
rules.instead: Choose one deliberate motion moment and respect reduced-motion preferences.

rules.dont: Headings barely bigger than the text (within 1.25× at every step).
rules.instead: Give heading levels a clear size and weight hierarchy.

rules.dont: A small, spaced-out uppercase label on its own line above a heading, or a small pill above the headline. Banned outright.
rules.instead: Put necessary context in the heading or supporting text.

rules.dont: Small numbers beside repeated section headings.
rules.instead: Use a deliberate, content-led alternative.

rules.dont: Colored glow shadows, a colored radial haze over a dark page, or a glow behind the hero.
rules.instead: Use restrained elevation or borders; no colored glow.

rules.dont: A thick colored border down one side of a card, or a thick accent border on a rounded card.
rules.instead: Use a deliberate, content-led alternative (a heading, an icon with a label, position).

rules.dont: A chunky sharp shadow offset 4px or more (unless the whole design is deliberately neobrutalist).
rules.instead: Use restrained elevation or borders.

rules.dont: Cards cut off at the screen edge, text hidden behind things, a lopsided first screen, text crammed against a box edge or the screen side, text spilling out of its box, headings floating between sections, lopsided headlines and one word alone on a last line.
rules.instead: Give text 12–16px of breathing room; let headings sit closer to what follows; balance the first screen.

rules.dont: Lines longer than about 80 characters; line spacing below 1.3; justified text full of gaps; paragraphs in capitals; letters spaced too far apart or squashed together; the same words three or more times in one card.
rules.instead: Aim for 65–75 characters per line and body line height of at least 1.3; normal case and tracking for body text.

rules.dont: Heading levels that jump, like H1 straight to H3.
rules.instead: Keep semantic heading levels consecutive.

rules.dont: Body text under 12px; buttons, links, menus or labels under 11px.
rules.instead: Use 16px body where practical, never below 12px; controls and labels at least 11px.

rules.dont: Orange arrows.
rules.instead: Use a restrained, consistent navigation icon treatment that fits the brand.

rules.dont: Two near-identical fonts (same letter structure) for headings and body. They look like a mistake.
rules.instead: Mix the structure: serif with sans, or a slab or mono with a plain sans. Contrast the letter structure, weight, width and size, and personality: one loud, one quiet.

rules.dont: Headline and body in the same weight, width and size range, so the page goes flat.
rules.instead: Vary weight, width and size: a heavy, wide or condensed headline over a regular body.

rules.dont: A pair whose lowercase height and width clash (a tiny x-height next to a big one).
rules.instead: Complement on proportions: similar x-height and width. Match the construction too: geometric with geometric, humanist with humanist.

rules.dont: A pair from clashing moods or eras, or one formal face with one relaxed one.
rules.instead: Match the mood and era, and the tone: both formal or both relaxed.

rules.dont: The expressive display face used for paragraphs, forms or buttons.
rules.instead: One personality, one workhorse: the expressive font only for headings and short labels; the quiet one for paragraphs, forms and buttons.

rules.dont: More than three font families, or a family with no clear role.
rules.instead: Give every font a job: headings, body, small labels. Two families are usually enough; three is the limit.

rules.dont: Font families typed as literals in components, with no heading and body tokens.
rules.instead: Use free Google Fonts and set a heading (display) token and a body token, then use the tokens everywhere.

rules.dont: Defaulting to Inter, Roboto, Poppins or Space Grotesk.
rules.instead: Choose the pairing for the brand under these rules. A default is only acceptable when the brand already mandates it, recorded in the pairing record.

rules.dont: Headings less than 1.25× the body size.
rules.instead: Keep a clear step: every heading level at least 1.25× the level below, and the main heading well above body.

rules.dont: Starting to build before a type pairing has been chosen and written down.
rules.instead: Before building, record the pairing: the display token and family, the body token and family, and why they pair under these rules (structure, weight/width/size, proportions, mood, one loud and one quiet). Format: a "Type pairing" section with Display:, Body: and Why: lines.

rules.dont: Keyboard-shortcut chips (⌘K) for shortcuts that do not exist, and middle dots used to fake a layout.
rules.instead: Show a shortcut only if it works; use spacing or a second line instead of dots.

rules.dont: Stock icon meanings: a lightning bolt for speed, a shield for security, sparkles for anything AI.
rules.instead: Pick icons that say something specific to this product, or write the capability in words.

rules.dont: Dot or graph-paper backgrounds used to look "technical", and glowing orbs standing in for a mascot.
rules.instead: Use a background that belongs to the brand, or a plain one. Draw a real mark or drop the orb.

rules.dont: transition: all as a reflex.
rules.instead: Transition only the properties that change.

rules.dont: A UI that looks like a famous product's design system, or one AI tool's default look traded for another's.
rules.instead: Build the look from this brand and its audience, and finish the choices the component kit left open.

rules.dont: Mixed casing (Title Case buttons beside sentence-case headings) and formula headlines: two clipped orders in a row ("Ship faster. Build smarter.") or matched number pairs ("Four projects, four problems").
rules.instead: Choose one casing (sentence case by default) and keep it. Write each heading as a plain statement of what follows.

rules.dont: Text selection, caret, scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset and tabular numerals left on browser defaults.
rules.instead: Theme them from the palette: the cheapest sign a page was built rather than assembled.

rules.dont: An italic serif hero headline by default, a full-sentence headline at display size, or tracking crushed past -0.04em.
rules.instead: Display type at most about 6rem, tracking no tighter than -0.04em, balanced heading wraps (text-wrap: balance; pretty for body).

rules.dont: Images with an empty, missing or placeholder source.
rules.instead: Use real images or leave the slot out.

rules.dont: A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.
rules.instead: Keep the task in the page flow.

rules.dont: Em dashes used to join clauses, or a spaced hyphen swapped in to get round the rule.
rules.instead: Rewrite the sentence with a comma, a colon, brackets or a full stop.

rules.dont: Copy that stages a reveal instead of saying the thing: a denial followed by the "real" point, a question answered in the next breath, a line that promises a secret, a run of short negatives ending in "just", or calling something "theater".
rules.instead: Put the point first, in one plain sentence.

rules.dont: Ending by asking for replies, opening by praising the question, piles of hashtags, and "thread" openers.
rules.instead: Stop on the last useful point and answer the substance. Two hashtags at most.

rules.dont: Headings that could sit over any section ("Final thoughts", "Conclusion"), headings phrased as questions, and bullets that open with a bolded label.
rules.instead: Write each heading as what the section shows. Write bullets as plain sentences.

rules.dont: Filler words that sound weighty and say nothing: delve, tapestry, testament, multifaceted, pivotal, realm, and "landscape" used as a metaphor.
rules.instead: Say the concrete thing. For long prose, also run a full writing linter.

rules.dont: Prose on autopilot: lists of three by habit, every sentence the same length, a run of clipped statements, hedging both ways, a new synonym for the same thing each time, and a sweeping last line.
rules.instead: Vary the rhythm, take a position, keep one word for one thing, and stop on the last concrete point.

rules.dont: Only the resting state was designed: no hover, focus, pressed, disabled, loading, error or empty state.
rules.instead: Design every state a control or view can be in, and look at each one rendered.

rules.dont: Buttons and links that do not say what happens: OK, Submit, Yes, No, Click here, Read more.
rules.instead: Name the action and its object (Save draft, Delete 3 files). Link text should make sense on its own.

rules.dont: Icon-only buttons and links with no name a screen reader can say, and images with no alt attribute.
rules.instead: Give every control a visible label or an aria-label, and every image an alt (empty for pure decoration).

rules.dont: Focus outlines switched off (outline: none) with nothing in their place, or tabindex above 0 scrambling the Tab order.
rules.instead: Keep a visible focus ring, styled from the palette. Use tabindex 0 or -1 only.

rules.dont: Errors that show a raw code or blame the person, spinners with no words, and progress bars that move whether or not work is happening.
rules.instead: Errors say what went wrong and how to fix it. Loading text names the real task. Show real progress or none.

rules.dont: Affordances added by habit: chevrons on rows that go nowhere, a green tick on every list item, every card lifting on hover, an icon beside every menu label.
rules.instead: Keep each one only where it means something: a chevron that opens, a tick in a real comparison, a lift on cards you can click.

rules.dont: An arrow after the words of every button and link.
rules.instead: Keep one arrow for the main action, or none.

rules.dont: Animation and transitions with no reduced-motion fallback.
rules.instead: Put non-essential motion inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), or turn it off under reduce.

rules.dont: Content that starts invisible (opacity 0 or pushed off screen) and only appears when a script or scroll reveal runs.
rules.instead: Render content visible by default and animate from a visible state, so a failed script never hides the page.

rules.dont: Animating width, height, top, left, margin or padding.
rules.instead: Animate transform and opacity instead, and keep the layout still.

rules.dont: Carousels, timed tabs, cards that tilt under the pointer, and loops that run past five seconds with no pause button.
rules.instead: Show items side by side or stacked, let people move things themselves, and give long loops a pause control.

rules.dont: Scroll-jacking, smooth-scroll libraries, whole-page scroll snapping and parallax on text.
rules.instead: Let the page scroll natively. If scroll-linked motion is the idea, keep it inside one section and record why.

rules.dont: Monospace type as a "technical" costume for headings or running text.
rules.instead: Keep monospace for code, data and measurements. Set prose and headings in the chosen display and body faces.

rules.dont: A new radius, font size or colour for each component: values typed by hand instead of taken from a scale.
rules.instead: Keep one radius scale, one type scale and one palette as tokens and use them everywhere. Add a step to a scale on purpose.

rules.dont: Highlighter marks or coloured bars behind words, and colour sprinkled inside headlines.
rules.instead: Show emphasis with weight, size or position. Use colour inside a word once a page at most.

rules.dont: Pure #000 text on light pages.
rules.instead: Use a near-black ink tinted toward the palette.

rules.dont: A dark mode made by flipping the light theme: flat surfaces, lost elevation, colours that buzz.
rules.instead: Design dark surfaces, elevation and contrast on their own terms, and check both themes.

rules.dont: Words baked into a picture: headlines, labels or charts saved as images.
rules.instead: Set every word as live text, so it can be read aloud, translated, zoomed and searched.

rules.dont: A page shipped without a language, a title, a viewport tag, a description or a share image.
rules.instead: Set <html lang>, <title>, the viewport meta, a meta description, a favicon and og:image before calling it done.

rules.dont: Console errors on load, or a script that fails and leaves part of the page dead.
rules.instead: Open the page with the console showing and fix every error before review.

rules.dont: A page that never shows the actual product, place or work: mood stock, a generic dashboard or a chat mock stands in for it.
rules.instead: Show the real thing at a readable size: the product's own screens, real photographs, or stand-ins listed for replacement.

rules.dont: A caption under every picture that explains or apologises for it.
rules.instead: Let the picture speak and put credits in one line at the end. Figures in reports keep their numbered captions.

rules.dont: Details made up to sound real: a room number, a batch code, '38% fewer re-runs', a founding story, opening hours or prices nobody supplied.
rules.instead: Use only details from the brief or a named source. Mark anything assumed and list it for the client.

rules.dont: The same voice for every client: warm, wry and a little literary, a dry one-liner closing each paragraph, a sign-off line in the footer, the brand name stretched into a running metaphor.
rules.instead: Choose a register for this client and reader, end paragraphs on information, and keep jokes for the small print.

rules.dont: Template lines that fit any business: "Say goodbye to", "Look no further", "Join thousands of", "Imagine a world where", "X made simple", "at your fingertips", "in just a few clicks".
rules.instead: Say what this business does, for whom, with one fact from the brief.

rules.dont: Inflated phrasing where a plain verb would do: "serves as", "stands as", "plays a key role", "in the heart of", "where X meets Y", "the world of".
rules.instead: Use is, has or does. Name the street or the thing.

rules.dont: An -ing clause tacked onto a fact to claim a meaning the text never shows (", ensuring a smooth start", ", highlighting our focus").
rules.instead: Say the concrete result, or stop at the fact.

rules.dont: Copy that talks about itself: "This section shows", "Below, you'll find", "Here are 5 reasons", or a colon set up as a reveal ("One thing changed:").
rules.instead: Give the content. Let the headings carry the structure.

rules.dont: Copy that calls itself honest, genuine or thoughtful, or announces its own frankness ("To be honest", "Let me be direct", "This is deliberate").
rules.instead: Show the quality with a fact or an admission. Give the reason instead of saying a choice was a choice.

rules.dont: Exclamation marks in body copy.
rules.instead: Let the words carry the energy. One exclamation mark in a long piece at most.

rules.dont: Long stand-ins for short words: "has the ability to", "due to the fact that", "at this point in time", "for the purpose of", "a large number of".
rules.instead: Use the short form: can, because, now, to, many.

rules.dont: Hedge on hedge ("arguably", "to some extent", "in many ways", "somewhat", "perhaps") until no claim is left.
rules.instead: Commit where the evidence is solid. Keep one plain qualifier where you really are unsure.

rules.dont: Claims resting on nameless authority: "studies show", "experts agree", "research suggests", "it is widely believed".
rules.instead: Name the study, person or dataset and its date, or drop the claim.

rules.dont: Sentences that open on stock connectors: Moreover, Furthermore, Additionally, Notably, Ultimately, Overall.
rules.instead: Let the logic join the sentences. Most of these words can go.

rules.dont: Ready-made openers and sign-offs: "Certainly!", "I hope this finds you well", "I hope this helps", "Do not hesitate to reach out".
rules.instead: Open with the point and close with the next step, or with nothing.

rules.dont: Three or more sentences in a row that start with the same words, for a drumroll.
rules.instead: Say it once and let the content build.

rules.dont: Long runs of bullets (eight or more in a row), and bullets for what is really one sentence.
rules.instead: Write prose where the ideas connect. Keep lists short and let items differ in length.

rules.dont: Every Heading Set In Title Case By Default.
rules.instead: Use sentence case for headings unless the brand's style guide says otherwise.

rules.dont: An opening paragraph of scene-setting before anything is said.
rules.instead: Start with the news. If the second paragraph works as the opener, cut the first.

rules.dont: Sentences that point back with a bare 'this' or 'that' at a whole earlier idea, things that act like people ('the data tells a story'), and passive voice that hides who acted.
rules.instead: Name the noun, and name the person or team who did it.

rules.dont: Comments that say what the next line plainly does: '// increment the counter' above count++, '# create user' above user = User().
rules.instead: Delete them. Keep comments that say why: a constraint, a workaround, a link to the decision.

rules.dont: Debug output left in: console.log, print('here'), debugger, breakpoint() and pdb calls.
rules.instead: Remove it, or send real messages through the project's logger. Command-line tools that print on purpose are fine.

rules.dont: Dead code: blocks commented out 'for later', lines after a return or throw, and branches behind if (false).
rules.instead: Delete it. Version control keeps the old code.

rules.dont: Error handling that hides failures: empty catch blocks, bare except or except: pass, .catch(() => {}), a catch that only logs and carries on, and try/catch or null checks wrapped round internal calls that cannot fail.
rules.instead: Catch only what you can handle, say why in a comment when you ignore an error on purpose, and let the rest fail loudly. Guard the real boundaries: user input, the network, files.

rules.dont: Layers nobody asked for: a function that only passes its arguments on to another, a class or factory with one caller, an interface with one implementation, settings for a value that never changes.
rules.instead: Call the real thing directly. Add a layer when a second use or a real seam needs it.

rules.dont: Names that say nothing: data, result, temp, obj, stuff, handleStuff, processData, helper.
rules.instead: Name the thing by what it holds or does: overdueLoans, parseInvoice, sendReminder.

rules.dont: Casts that change nothing or silence the type checker: as any, as unknown as T, String() round a string, Boolean(!!x), str() round a string literal, list(list(x)).
rules.instead: Fix the type where it starts and drop the cast. Where a cast is needed, cast once, to the narrowest type.

rules.dont: any as the type of choice: : any, any[], Record<string, any>, -> Any.
rules.instead: Write the real type, or use unknown and narrow it with a check.

rules.dont: TODO and placeholder residue: vague TODOs with no owner or ticket ('TODO: add error handling'), '... rest of the code here', 'implement this', and stubs that throw 'Not implemented' on paths people use.
rules.instead: Finish it, or turn the TODO into a ticket and link it. Never ship a stub on a path people use.

rules.dont: New code that ignores the file round it: tabs among spaces, single quotes among double, var among const, snake_case among camelCase.
rules.instead: Match the surrounding file and the project's formatter, even where you prefer another style.

rules.dont: Imports that nothing in the file uses.
rules.instead: Delete them. Keep side-effect imports (styles, polyfills) and deliberate re-exports.

rules.dont: Pyramids of nested if, for and try, five or more levels deep.
rules.instead: Return early, pull a block into a named function, or turn the condition round.

rules.dont: Long docstrings and JSDoc blocks on trivial functions that only restate the name and the arguments.
rules.instead: Keep a docstring when it says something the signature cannot: units, side effects, errors, a surprising rule.

rules.dont: Errors thrown with a message that names no cause: 'Something went wrong', 'Error', 'Failed', 'Invalid input'.
rules.instead: Give each failure a stable code and a plain message that says what failed and what to do next.

rules.dont: Working notes committed with the change: NOTES.md, PLAN.md, SCRATCH.md, TODO.md, IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md.
rules.instead: Keep notes out of the repo, or fold what matters into the README, the docs or the pull request.

rules.dont: A diff that does more than was asked: drive-by refactors, renamed files, new dependencies, reformatted lines and features nobody requested.
rules.instead: Keep the change to the task. Raise the other ideas on their own, as separate changes.

rules.dont: Tests that mock so much they test nothing real: four or more patches on one test, assertions about the mocks themselves, snapshots nobody reads.
rules.instead: Test behaviour through real code paths, and mock only slow or outside boundaries.

rules.dont: Controls wired to nothing: href="#", javascript:void(0), buttons with no handler, toggles that do not save.
rules.instead: Make every visible control do something, or leave it out until it does.

rules.dont: Real-looking navigation that leads to 'Coming soon', 'Under construction' or a blank page.
rules.instead: Ship the link with the page. Until then, leave it out, or show it disabled with the reason.

rules.dont: Status messages that say nothing: 'Something went wrong', 'An error occurred', 'Oops!', 'No items to display', 'Invalid input'.
rules.instead: Say what happened and what to do next ('Could not save: you are offline. Your draft is kept.'). Empty states name the next step.

rules.dont: Hand-styled raw buttons, inputs and cards beside the project's own components, or call sites that override a shared component's colour, radius, spacing or focus style.
rules.instead: Use the shared component and its variants. If a variant is missing, add it to the component once instead of styling round it.

rules.dont: Delete and other actions that cannot be undone run on one click, with no confirm and no undo, styled like the main action and sitting beside it.
rules.instead: Confirm or offer undo in proportion to the damage, use the danger style, and keep it apart from the main action.

rules.dont: Clicks with no visible response: a submit button that stays live during the request so a double click sends twice, no pressed state, a save that succeeds in silence, a toast that never closes.
rules.instead: Respond within about 100 ms: disable and relabel the button while it works, confirm success briefly, and close toasts after a few seconds.

rules.dont: One thing called by a new name in every sentence (the tool, the platform, the solution, the app), so readers wonder if there are four.
rules.instead: Pick one name and keep it.

rules.dont: Ranges that are not ranges: 'everything from startups to global enterprises', 'from design to delivery and everything in between'.
rules.instead: List what is actually covered, or name the one thing that matters.

rules.dont: Bold sprinkled through paragraphs: three or more bold phrases in one paragraph, every name and number in bold.
rules.instead: Bold one thing per section at most: the thing a skimming reader must not miss.

rules.dont: Disclaimers about the writer's own limits: 'as of my last update', 'while specific details are limited', 'I do not have real-time access'.
rules.instead: Find the source and cite it with its date, or leave the claim out.

rules.dont: Endings that could close any piece: 'The future looks bright', 'Only time will tell', 'It remains to be seen', 'Exciting times ahead'.
rules.instead: End on the last concrete point, a date, or the next step.

rules.dont: Long or abstract words where a plain one exists: utilize, leverage, facilitate, commence, prior to, in order to, numerous, synergy, north star, flywheel, substrate.
rules.instead: Use the plain word (use, help, start, before, to, many), and name the concrete thing instead of the metaphor.

rules.dont: Brochure adjectives: vibrant, breathtaking, stunning, renowned, iconic, groundbreaking, must-visit.
rules.instead: Describe what is there: the view, the size, the year it opened.

rules.dont: The challenge formula: 'Despite these challenges, it continues to thrive.'
rules.instead: Name the actual problem and the actual result, with numbers if you have them.

rules.dont: Tap targets smaller than 44 by 44 px, or packed closer than 8 px apart: icon buttons, small chips, close crosses.
rules.instead: Make every control at least 44 px each way (pad the hit area if the icon is smaller) and leave 8 px between controls.

rules.dont: Inputs, selects and text areas with no label at all.
rules.instead: Give each field a visible label tied to it with for and id, or wrap it in the label. Use aria-label only when a visible label truly cannot fit.

rules.dont: Email and phone fields typed as plain text, and autocomplete switched off on name, email, phone and address fields.
rules.instead: Use type="email" and type="tel" so phones show the right keyboard, and set autocomplete values so browsers can fill the form.

rules.dont: A viewport tag that stops people zooming: user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1.
rules.instead: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and let people zoom.

rules.dont: Form fields set under 16px, so phones zoom the page when you tap into one.
rules.instead: Set inputs, selects and text areas at 16px or more.

rules.dont: Form errors that are hard to find or fix: one message at the top of a long form, a red border with no words, checks only on submit, errors screen readers never hear, required fields not marked.
rules.instead: Put the message next to the field and say how to fix it, check when a field is left, move focus to the first error, announce it (role="alert" or aria-live), and mark required fields.

rules.dont: Navigation that is hard to use: more than five items in a bottom or tab bar, icon-only items with no words, no sign of the current page, a menu that moves between pages, modals used for main navigation.
rules.instead: Five items at most in a bottom bar, each icon with a label, the current page marked (aria-current="page"), and the menu in the same place on every page.

rules.dont: Charts that hide their data: a pie or donut with more than five slices, red against green as the only difference, axes with no units, a legend far from its lines, gridlines louder than the data, thousands of raw points.
rules.instead: Match the chart to the question (a line for a trend, bars to compare), label lines directly, give units, keep gridlines faint, use shapes or labels as well as colour, and aggregate big sets.

rules.dont: Charts drawn in canvas or SVG with no text a screen reader can read, and no table or summary of what they show.
rules.instead: Give each chart a title and a one-line summary of its point (aria-label or a caption), and put a table of the numbers nearby.

rules.dont: Pages that jump while they load: images with no width and height or aspect ratio, web fonts with no font-display, content that pushes the page down when it arrives.
rules.instead: Reserve the space: set width and height (or aspect-ratio) on images, use font-display: swap, and size placeholders to the content.

rules.dont: Full-screen sections set to height: 100vh, which runs under the address bar on phones.
rules.instead: Use 100dvh (with 100vh before it as a fallback), or min-height instead of height.

rules.dont: z-index values like 999 or 9999 typed to win a fight.
rules.instead: Keep a short layer scale as tokens (base, dropdown, sticky, overlay, modal, toast) and use it.

rules.dont: Actions that only appear on hover, so people on touch screens and keyboards never see them.
rules.instead: Show the action, or also reveal it on :focus-within and on tap.

rules.dont: Interface transitions slower than half a second, or exits as slow as entrances.
rules.instead: Keep small transitions around 150 to 300 ms, and let exits run a little faster than entrances.

rules.dont: No skip link on a page with a long menu, drag and drop with no keyboard way, and focus left behind when a view or dialog changes.
rules.instead: Add a skip link to the main content, give every drag a button or keyboard route, and move focus to the new view, dialog or first error.

rules.dont: Status, errors or chart series told apart by colour alone: a red border, a green dot, a red line beside a green one.
rules.instead: Pair colour with a word, an icon or a shape.

rules.dont: A bot presented as a person: a human name and photo with no sign the replies are automated.
rules.instead: Say plainly that the replies come from an AI model, and offer a way to reach a person.

rules.dont: Dates that read two ways, like 03/04/2026.
rules.instead: Write the month as a word (3 April 2026), or use ISO dates (2026-04-03) in data.

rules.dont: Straight quote marks and apostrophes (' and ") in text people read on a page, slide or document.
rules.instead: Use curly quotes and apostrophes in visible text. Keep straight quotes in code, Markdown source, commands and attributes.

done_checklist.check: On a phone (390px wide): nothing scrolls sideways, the main button is easy to find, and buttons and links are big enough to tap (at least 44px).
At first glance: someone can tell what the page is for and what to click within five seconds.
Colour: nothing relies on colour alone to make sense, so it still works in grayscale. Text is readable against its background (at least 4.5:1), including text on photos and coloured buttons.
Empty and error moments: a failed form shows a clear message and keeps what was typed, and anything that can be empty shows something useful instead of a blank space.
Keyboard: every button and link can be reached with Tab, and you can see which one is selected.
Code: it builds, the type check and the tests pass, and the diff touches only what was asked for.
Then say what you checked and what you couldn't check.
